experiment.name: Human severity-mechanism proteins in the B. rossi serum proteome: complicated against uncomplicated (DS07)
experiment.description: Do serum proteins of mechanisms linked to severity in human disease (haemolysis and haem scavenging, neutrophil granule proteins, fibrinolysis and anticoagulants, complement regulation) differ between complicated and uncomplicated B. rossi babesiosis in DS07? Hypothesis: at least one mechanism candidate differs at q < 0.05.
experiment.summary: None of the 10 family proteins differs at q < 0.05 between 14 complicated and 18 uncomplicated dogs (9 tested; 2 with p < 0.05). The smallest p is haemoglobin beta: Cliff's delta +0.48 (+0.09 to +0.82), p 0.019, q 0.133. Positive controls lactoferrin and CD14 are higher in complicated dogs, as CB112 reported. 9 tests, 0 passed at q < 0.05.

payload.headline: None of the 10 family proteins differs at q < 0.05 between 14 complicated and 18 uncomplicated dogs (9 tested; 2 with p < 0.05). The smallest p is haemoglobin beta: Cliff's delta +0.48 (+0.09 to +0.82), p 0.019, q 0.133.
caveats: One proteome, one source (SRC-C), no replication.
The complicated label includes anaemia and laboratory thresholds: haemoglobin and haptoglobin partly restate it.
No covariates (age, sex, treatment, time from onset, sample haemolysis) are in the files.
Detectable effect about 1.0 SD at alpha 0.05, about 1.3 SD after correction for 10 tests.

payload.footnote: DS07, SRC-C, B. rossi: 14 complicated vs 18 uncomplicated dogs; one species, one source. Value: log2 ratio to the plex's pooled standard. p: labels permuted inside each plex (10,000 permutations, seed 20261112); interval: 2,000 bootstrap resamples of dogs within each group. q: Benjamini-Hochberg over 10 proteins (an untested protein counts in the family size). Lactoferrin and CD14 are positive controls (CB112 reported them higher in complicated dogs).
Each point is one dog (log2 ratio to the plex standard). A missing value is missing for the whole plex. Controls are shown for context and are not in the primary test.

S1 unstratified permutation; S2 leave-one-plex-out range of delta; S3 infected (32) vs controls (20), plex-stratified, not corrected; S5 Spearman rho with haemoglobin beta among infected dogs. Not in the family.

Haemoglobin alpha fails the master-protein check: P60529 is a candidate only and its group master J9NXL3 (LOC100855558, 'Uncharacterized protein') has no stated identity. Outside the family; no claim.

sections.heading: Question
paragraphs: Do serum proteins of mechanisms linked to severity in human malaria, human babesiosis and sepsis (haemolysis and haem scavenging, neutrophil granule proteins and histones, fibrinolysis and anticoagulant consumption, complement regulation) differ between complicated and uncomplicated B. rossi babesiosis in the one public canine serum proteome (DS07)?
Hypothesis: at least one mechanism candidate (not a positive control) differs at q < 0.05.

sections.heading: What was done
paragraphs: The 11 proteins were fixed by the package file and mapped to accessions by part a. Before the outcome lock opened, each was checked as a master protein in B_Proteins.txt. Haemoglobin alpha failed: its group master has no stated identity. It was dropped from the family and is shown once as a secondary result. Haptoglobin is quantified through its group master A0A5F4DB38, which has the haptoglobin gene symbol LOC479668. The family has 10 proteins.

For each protein: Cliff's delta, complicated against uncomplicated, on the log2 ratio to the plex standard; a permutation p with labels permuted inside each of the 11 TMT plexes (10,000 permutations, seed 20261112); a 95% bootstrap interval (2,000 resamples of dogs); Benjamini-Hochberg over 10 proteins.

Missing values in DS07 are missing for a whole plex. So a presence test only tests how the groups were placed in plexes. Proteins seen in less than 60% of a group were therefore tested on the observed dogs only and flagged as low coverage. A protein with fewer than 3 observed dogs in a group was not tested: Histone H4 (4 complicated, 2 uncomplicated, plexes B1, B9).

sections.heading: Result
paragraphs: None of the 10 family proteins differs at q < 0.05 between 14 complicated and 18 uncomplicated dogs (9 tested; 2 with p < 0.05). The smallest p is haemoglobin beta: Cliff's delta +0.48 (+0.09 to +0.82), p 0.019, q 0.133.

Positive controls: lactoferrin delta +0.42 (+0.01 to +0.81) and CD14 +0.42 (+0.05 to +0.74) are both higher in complicated dogs, the direction CB112 reported for the same data. The value pipeline is consistent with the source article. Neither control passes the family correction (q 0.133 and 0.242).

Mechanism candidates: haemoglobin beta is higher in complicated dogs (delta +0.48, +0.09 to +0.82; Hodges-Lehmann shift +1.17 log2 units; p 0.019, q 0.133). Its interval excludes zero but it does not pass the correction, and it partly restates the label. S100A8 points the same way (delta +0.42, -0.10 to +0.93, n 10 vs 16). Haptoglobin +0.08, alpha-2-antiplasmin +0.10, protein C +0.02 (low coverage, n 7 vs 9), antithrombin -0.08 and factor H -0.12: all intervals include zero. Histone H4 could not be tested.

Checks: leave-one-plex-out never changes the sign of the haemoglobin beta, lactoferrin, CD14 or S100A8 deltas. The unstratified test gives p < 0.05 for Haemoglobin beta, CD14. Against controls, Antithrombin (SERPINC1) (-0.67), CD14 (+0.83), Lactoferrin (+0.44) differ at p < 0.05. Of these, Antithrombin (SERPINC1), CD14 do not differ by complicated status (p >= 0.05): they move with infection more than with complicated disease. Among infected dogs, Haptoglobin (group master A0A5F4DB38) (rho +0.58), Lactoferrin (rho +0.54), Protein C (rho +0.51), CD14 (rho +0.46) rise with haemoglobin beta.

sections.heading: What this does not show
paragraphs: A null here is 'not shown', not 'absent': with 14 against 18 dogs the test detects about 1.0 SD at alpha 0.05 and about 1.3 SD after correction.

DS07 is one source with no replication. It has no covariates (age, sex, treatment, time from onset, sample haemolysis index), and its label is defined partly by haematocrit, urea, creatinine, bilirubin, glucose and lactate. A haemoglobin difference may come from in-vivo haemolysis, anaemia severity or haemolysis of the stored sample, and these cannot be told apart.

Serum proteomics measures total protein, not activity. Alpha-2-antiplasmin and protein C amounts do not test fibrinolytic shutdown or protein C activation. Haptoglobin was measured as total haptoglobin group abundance, not as free haptoglobin. This is not a screen of the proteome, and no protein outside the fixed family was looked at.
